doc.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: Playing old records for Louis Metcalf
summary: Louie Bacon denies he is the trumpeter on a Bessie Smith record; Vollmer works out it is Louis Metcalf, who admits it.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: different. And Bacon said, “That’s me there.” So and I remember I played the record for a whole week and tried to figure out who can that trumpeter be. And finally I hit, I said I think it might be Louis Metcalf. Well luckily I was into this early enough, Louis Metcalf was still alive and around, and I sort of knew him. And I asked him to come to the house, and I played him “In the House Blues.” And he said, “Yes, I have to admit, that’s me.” But, in other words he didn’t think much of it, although it’s great trumpeting. He said, “You have to understand I was playing the music of the time.” They would call you up and they would say, “Can you growl?” And you’d say yes, and you got the job.
